Also inspect `test_session_get_adapter_prefix_matching_mixed_case` and `test_session_get_adapter_prefix_matching_is_case_insensitive`, which test matching and differently cased URLs [Data: Entities 1266, 1267, 1276; Relationships 2056, 2058, 2081]. A case-sensitive change requires reviewing prefix comparison and these tests. A shortest-prefix-first change requires reviewing the selection loop's traversal and comparison rule. The evidence establishes only that the more-specific prefix currently takes precedence, not how the loop implements it.\n\n**Send call sites.** No `send` method, caller, module location, or call site appears in the supplied summaries. No exact send location can therefore be named. As a proposed search plan, trace paths that obtain an adapter through `get_adapter` and then invoke transport sending. Verify that changed matching reaches the same adapter/send behavior, and check whether direct `Session.send` paths bypass lookup. This is a search plan, not an established source fact.\n\n**Limits.** The records contain test descriptions and external method names, but no implementation, execution results, or line numbers [Data: Entities 1261-1267, 1276-1277; Relationships 2035, 2039, 2042, 2056, 2058, 2081-2082].", 'Mounted adapter prefixes are stored as keys in the session\'s `adapters` mapping, initialized as an `OrderedDict`. The ordered mapping preserves prefix registration order and is inspected with `list(s.adapters)` in `test_transport_adapter_ordering` [Data: Sources (91); Entities (107)].\n\nThe supplied evidence shows this in `tests/test_requests.py`, within `test_transport_adapter_ordering`: prefixes such as `"http://git"` and `"http://github.com/about/"` are mounted, and the resulting adapter-key order is asserted. It also shows that `s2.adapters` can be replaced with a regular dictionary before mounting another adapter [Data: Sources (91)]. The `Session` implementation that initializes `self.adapters` is not included in the snapshot, so the exact implementation location cannot be determined from the supplied evidence.', "The supported path is in `src/requests/sessions.py`, within `Session.request` (in the supplied range `L569-L717`). It prepares the request, merges environment settings, and calls `self.send(prep, **send_kwargs)`. The convenience methods `get`, `options`, `head`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, and `delete` all route into `request`, so they can reach this call site [Data: Sources (56)].\n\nInside `Session.send`, the adapter is looked up with `self.get_adapter(url=request.url)`, after which the request is sent through the selected adapter via `adapter.send(request, **kwargs)`. The supplied evidence therefore shows a `Session.request` -> `Session.send` -> `Session.get_adapter` -> `adapter.send` path; it does not show any code path that calls `Session.send` after completing adapter lookup. The adapter lookup occurs inside `Session.send`, before the adapter's `send` call [Data: Sources (56); Entities (812, 24); Relationships (1105)].\n\nThe snapshot does not provide additional callers of `Session.send` beyond this request/convenience-method path, nor does it establish concrete runtime bindings for unresolved receiver calls.", "No—not in the standard `Session.send` implementation shown. A direct call such as `s.send(...)` enters `Session.send`, which first selects an adapter with `self.get_adapter(url=request.url)` and then calls `adapter.send(request, **kwargs)`. Therefore, changing adapter matching would affect direct `Session.send` calls through this lookup. [Data: Sources (56); Entities (24, 1113)]\n\nThe evidence does not establish the concrete runtime class behind every receiver written as `s.send(...)`, nor whether a subclass or custom session overrides `send` or `get_adapter`. Such calls could therefore bypass this specific lookup only if they use a different implementation. The supplied snapshot also identifies the `SEND` -> `ADAPTER.SEND` call relationship, but does not show another direct path that bypasses `get_adapter`. [Data: Relationships (1105); Entities (1117, 389)]\n\nFor the stated matching-change investigation, inspect `Session.send` in `src/requests/sessions.py` at the supplied `send` definition, especially its `self.get_adapter(...)` lookup and subsequent `adapter.send(...)` call. Also inspect any custom or overridden `send` implementations and the registration logic that populates the session's adapters; the snapshot names relevant mount and prefix-matching tests but does not provide their source locations. [Data: Sources (56); Entities (1261, 1263, 1266, 1267)]", '## Adapter-key ordering assertions\n\nIn `tests/test_requests.py`, within `test_transport_adapter_ordering`, the initial assertion requires a new session\'s adapter keys to be ordered as `["https://", "http://"]`:\n\n```python\norder = ["https://", "http://"]\nassert order == list(s.adapters)\n```\n\nAfter mounting `http://git`, `http://github`, `http://github.com`, and `http://github.com/about/`, the test asserts longest/more-specific prefixes first, followed by the default HTTPS and HTTP keys:\n\n```python\nassert order == list(s.adapters)\n```\n\nwith the expected order being `http://github.com/about/`, `http://github.com`, `http://github`, `http://git`, `https://`, and `http://`. It then mounts the `gittip` variants and makes another `assert order == list(s.adapters)`, expecting each group to remain ordered from the most specific key to the least specific key, followed by `https://` and `http://`. [Data: Sources (91); Entities (1261)]\n\nThe test also checks that replacing `s2.adapters` with an HTTP mapping and then mounting HTTPS retains both `"http://"` and `"https://"`, but those are membership assertions rather than adapter-key ordering assertions. ## Registration Order

Inspect `requests.Session.mount`, specifically the ordering structure updated when adapters are registered. Mounted prefixes are stored as keys in the session’s `adapters` mapping, initialized as an `OrderedDict`; registration order and key retention are checked in `test_transport_adapter_ordering` in `tests/test_requests.py` [Data: Sources (91); Entities (107, 1261); Relationships (2035, 2039)].

Verify that a matching change preserves the expected ordering: more-specific prefixes precede less-specific prefixes, followed by `"https://"` and `"http://"`. Also check the case-focused tests that mount mixed-case prefixes before lookup, and confirm that both default mappings remain present when the adapters mapping is replaced with a regular dictionary [Data: Sources (91); Entities (1266, 1267, 1277); Relationship (2082)].

## Selection Loop

Inspect `requests.Session.get_adapter`, especially its prefix-comparison logic and traversal order. For a case-sensitive change, review the comparison used for URLs and adapter prefixes against `test_session_get_adapter_prefix_matching_mixed_case` and `test_session_get_adapter_prefix_matching_is_case_insensitive`. For a shortest-prefix-first change, review the loop’s traversal and comparison rule against `test_session_get_adapter_prefix_matching`, which covers general, more-specific, and nonmatching prefixes [Data: Entity (1263); Entities (1266, 1267, 1276); Relationships (2042, 2056, 2058, 2081)].

The evidence establishes that the more-specific prefix currently takes precedence, but it does not show the implementation of the loop, its exact source line, or whether the current behavior is implemented by iteration order, explicit comparison, or another mechanism [Data: Entities (1261-1267, 1276-1277); Relationships (2035, 2039, 2042, 2056, 2058, 2081-2082)].

## Send Call Sites

The supported production path is `src/requests/sessions.py`: `Session.request` prepares the request and calls `self.send(prep, **send_kwargs)` within the supplied range `L569-L717`. `Session.send` then calls `self.get_adapter(url=request.url)` and sends through the selected adapter with `adapter.send(request, **kwargs)` [Data: Sources (56); Entities (812, 24); Relationships (1105)].

Therefore, inspect `Session.send` at its `get_adapter` lookup and subsequent `adapter.send` call. Direct `Session.send` calls do not bypass this lookup in the standard implementation shown; they also select an adapter before sending. The supplied evidence does not establish other `Session.send` callers, concrete runtime receiver classes, or subclass/custom overrides, so those would need to be searched separately [Data: Sources (56); Entities (24, 1113, 1117, 389); Relationships (1105)].

The exact implementation location of `Session.mount`, the full `get_adapter` source, and any additional send call sites are not provided by the snapshot. Searching for custom or overridden `mount`, `get_adapter`, or `send` implementations is consequently a proposed investigation plan, not an established source fact.
